subject: Adaptor version handoff proposal and compatibility SLAs
messages:
From: Anna Park <anna@uiforge.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: eng@uiforge.com
Date: Sun, 01 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: UIForge adaptor changes we need from Redwood (compat + timeline)

Marcus —

Thanks again for the briefing last week. We did a deeper pass with the integration team and have a concrete set of changes that will land in UIForge's 3.0 release (targeting Dec). The changes touch the Redwood adaptor surface in two places:

- auth header normalization (we will move to token-prefix-less Authorization in a couple endpoints)
- streaming payload framing (slight schema change when we emit partial chunks)
- new model aliasing behavior: UIForge will prefer model: "rwd-opt-1" aliases instead of raw model ids in our config

Those are breaking for the current adaptor implementation and will require either (A) Redwood to accept backward-compatible routing for a short window, or (B) UIForge to maintain dual adaptor tags for a transition period. Both options have costs for us.

Can you share Redwood's recommended deprecation cadence, and whether you can provide an automated migration (CLI or endpoint) that renames/rewrites calls on our behalf? Attached is a short summary and a compatibility matrix so you can see the exact endpoints.

Proposed constraints from our side:
- a 60-day grace/dual-support window after Redwood's cutover
- a weekly canary window to validate streaming framing changes in production

We'd like to lock a plan by Monday (Nov 2) so engineering can schedule the 3.0 branch.

Thanks —
Anna Park
Head of Integrations, UIForge
anna@uiforge.com

Attachments: uiforge-adaptor-change-summary.xlsx, compat_matrix.csv
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Park <anna@uiforge.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: UIForge adaptor changes we need from Redwood (compat + timeline)

Anna —

Appreciate the clear matrix and early heads-up. Quick notes from our side after an internal sync:

- We can offer an automated migration tool that rewrites the Authorization header expectation and will provide a small proxy shim for streaming framing differences. That tool will live as a short-lived compatibility layer in Redwood Dedicated/Private customers and as a small client-side CLI for hosted integrations.
- We are comfortable committing to a 45-day dual-support window (noting that a longer window increases operational cost on our routing layer). If UIForge needs 60 days strictly, we can make a case to extend to 60 days for this partner (requires sign-off from Ops).
- For model aliasing, we can accept both aliases and raw ids for a 90-day migration period and will add an opt-in flag to the adaptor API to prefer aliases immediately.

Action items I propose: 
1) Redwood provides the auto-migrate CLI + a playbook (we'll attach the draft) by EOD Wednesday (Nov 4).
2) We stand up a 2-hour weekly canary window for you starting Nov 9 to validate streaming framing.
3) Decision on 45 vs 60 day grace window — I will loop in Ops (cc: vanessa) and get a final answer by Wednesday.

Can you confirm the weekly canary weekday/time that works for your on-call? Also, please confirm if you need RFC-style notarization or DocuSign for the migration extension (some partners want that as a record).

I'll attach the draft migration playbook to this thread.

— Marcus Lin
Partner Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-auto-migration-playbook.pdf
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Anna Park <anna@uiforge.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: UIForge adaptor changes we need from Redwood (compat + timeline)

Looping in operations and product perspective. A few operational constraints and a recommended path: 

- Ops note: sustained dual-support windows > 60 days materially increase routing and KV-cache pressure. We can approve 60 days as an exception for strategic partners but need a written migration plan and a milestone checkpoint at day 30.
- Product note: for streaming framing, we'd prefer to do an opt-in rollout where UIForge explicitly opts into the new framing header via a feature flag; this avoids accidental breakage for other partners.
- Legal/Finance: if UIForge requests a contract addendum for extended support, we will require a short SOW; ask Anna if they need a SOW or just a signed agreement.

Proposed refined timeline: 
- Nov 4: Redwood sends CLI + playbook (Marcus)
- Nov 9–Dec 21: Canary windows weekly (2 hours each)
- Nov 30: 30-day checkpoint (technical sign-off)
- Jan 1: Final cutover (if both sides complete migration steps)

If UIForge needs the 60-day requirement explicitly in writing for procurement, we can provide a short addendum (simple one-pager). Otherwise, we keep it as a mutual operational commitment.

-Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships Operations, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
From: Anna Park <anna@uiforge.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, eng@uiforge.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: UIForge adaptor changes we need from Redwood (compat + timeline)

Marcus / Vanessa / Laura —

Thanks for the quick turn. This plan looks workable for us. We accept the 60-day exception and appreciate the migration tooling + playbook. A couple quick confirmations: 

- Weekly canary window: Tuesdays 09:00–11:00 PT works for our on-call (starting Nov 9).
- We will sign a short SOW addendum that states a 60-day dual-support window and the milestone checkpoint on Nov 30. Please send the addendum to procurement@uiforge.com.
- We will plan to migrate alias usage by Dec 15 and will use the opt-in feature-flag for streaming framing during canaries.

Can we schedule a 30-min kick-off on Nov 5 to walk the migration playbook and CLI? If so, please propose two time slots.

Thanks —
Anna
Head of Integrations, UIForge
anna@uiforge.com
